recipes.name: Margaret’s Keftedes (Greek Meatballs)
ingredients_raw: 4 slices white bread, torn into pieces

steps.text: Moisten the bread pieces with the milk in a large bowl, and set aside.
Mince the garlic in a food processor, then add the onion, mint, salt, and pepper. Process until the onion is finely chopped.
Add the onion mixture to the bowl with the moist bread, along with the beef, lamb, and eggs. Mix with your hands until thoroughly blended.
Roll the mixture into balls measuring 1 1/2 to 2 inches in diameter.

Place the flour in a shallow pan, and roll the balls in the flour to coat. Shake off any excess flour, and place the meatballs onto a plate or baking sheet, pressing to flatten slightly. This will keep them from rolling away.
Heat 1 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the meatballs, 8 or 10 at a time, and cook until nicely browned on the outside, and no longer pink in the center, about 10 minutes.
Drain meatballs on a paper towel-lined plate. Repeat with remaining meatballs.

raw_recipe.headline: Margaret’s Keftedes (Greek Meatballs)
raw_recipe.description: This is my yia yia’s recipe--a family favorite straight from the village of Kyparissia. Serve as an appetizer or with tzatziki, Greek salata, and pita or pasta for a full meal. They taste best served at room temp and make for wonderful leftovers. If you don’t care for lamb, try using all beef instead.

review.reviewBody: This was a great recipe but I made a few changes to suit our tastes. First it is very important to soak the milk in bread as suggested. Also, make sure to grate the onion right into the bowl so you can integrate the juice from the grated onion. I used a generous amount of parsely instead of the mint. I skipped dredging in flour and instead used olive oil for health purposes. These are a hit every time!!!

These were fantastic! I was having company for a greek dinner and made these meatballs in addition to chicken. I read the reviews so I also made a few changes. Double the meat quantity, but still only used 2 eggs, in addition to the mint I added 4 t. of greek seasoning. Since I baked them instead of frying, did not roll in flour. Everyone was raving about these! Will definitely make again!

Oh yeah; making these again. I took reviewer "Jimmy's" advice and cut the eggs to one per pound of meat. Since it's summer, to keep the kitchen cool I put them in a grill pan and grilled them over smoldering rosemary stalks. To keep them gluten-free for our family, I subbed 2 Lundberg's rice cakes for the bread. : )

I made a few substitutions based on what I had on hand, and from the suggestions of other reviewers. I used all ground lamb, 4 slices of multigrain bread, a handful of finely chopped fresh mint, 4 minced cloves garlic, and reduced the eggs to just 2. I skipped the flour dredge and simply baked the meatballs on a rimmed baking sheet at 350 for 20 minutes, flipped them, then baked another 20 minutes. Gave them a quick sprinkle of chopped parsley once they came out of the oven. The meatballs were absolutely delicious! Baking them and skipping the flour dredge made for a relatively fast preparation too! I would absolutely make these again! They are fantastic served on pita with tzaziki sauce and fresh vegetables! Thank you so much for the recipe!

Wonderful - I love authentic redipes such as this. Because my computer was down a while tonight i made something very similar off top of head: used 1 pd. ground beef, 1 pound ground lamb, 1/2 tsp nutmeg, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp saffron. 1/2 tsp tumeric, 1/2 diced red onioon and 4 minced garlic cloves. Baked in 375 oven for 45 minutes. heavenly and yummy result. Served in Pita Bread with Hummus and olives and greens and tomatoes. Great!

Like others I had to do my own thing with recipe as guidance. I forgot to check needed items in recipe when I went grocery shopping. Recognized the eggs, bread amounts were too much, I decided to make a double batch of these morsels & use 2 pounds of ground beef. Determined not to make another trip required substitutes. We don’t eat white bread so I used dried unseasoned bread crumbs (1 cup = 4 slices bread) and no onion I gave it a healthy dose of onion powder, a tsp of garlic & herb grilling spice, a Tbsp of German beef flavoring, and a good dash of paprika. Because of the dried bread I used 1 cup of 1/2 & 1/2 and all 4 eggs (mine are jumbo size) to help reconstitute the bread crumbs. Baked in oven so I did not roll them in the flour. Sorry folks, but there are times we just want to get it put together with what’s on hand. If you are a seasoned cook/baker you can make it work regardless. The 4 stars are for my altering original recipe. They were good.

Yummy! These were so delicious and everybody ate them (picky hubby, 5 year old, 15 month old and me!). I used 1 pound of ground beef since our commissary doesn't carry lamb, and only 2 eggs. I also played with the seasonings a bit, used more mint, parsley, oregano and marjoram. I baked them in the oven and served them on pitas with tzatziki sauce, sliced tomatoes, olives, and feta cheese. We will definitely be having these again, thanks for sharing the recipe.

Wow, so good!!! I used the food processor to chop out the bread into crumbs. And I drained the moisture from the other food processor mix before adding it to the bowl with the bread. I also added 1cup flour to make burger patties instead of meatballs. The burgers are so flavorful and wonderful. Love how the freeze-dried mint shines through at just the right amount. Ate these as burgers with lettuce, tomato, feta and tzatziki sauce. Incredible, thank you!!

I made a few changes, like I added oregano and used garlic powder, and used seasoned bread crumbs instead of plain bread soaked in milk and left out the eggs, and cooked them in the oven at 350 until they reached an internal temp of 155 or higher, they turned out AWESOME!

so good! i doubled the bread, milk, garlic, and onions. only put in 2 eggs.... i flattened them coz i was worried they wont be cooked from the inside.. turned out great! used the leftovers in pasta with cream sauce!
i experimented with a few in the oven, but the fried ones were so much better !

These are really good. I'm giving them four stars because I changed several things. I used all ground beef, plus fresh mint and also added some fresh marjarom, since I had it. For the bread I used some herbed black olive bread that I had on hand, and I only used one egg for about a pound of meat. I started soaking the bread in the milk, then threw it in the food processor along with the salt and pepper, herbs, and garlic. This made a little bread 'paste' that I then added to the meat with the egg. I used about a teaspoon of salt for one pound of meat.
great but def reduce eggs to two and not so much bread add some Greek oregano and crumbled feta into mixture, takes it to a higher level!

Way too many eggs! The mix turned into egg & meat soup! I had to go to the store for another pound of beef after adding the eggs. I could see that it was never going to form together into meatballs, it was just too soupy...
They did not use some vinegar and slight bit of browning sauce for color or flavor.And i usually kick in a small bit of bullion if it’s lame hamburger.But mostly just vinegar is missing.
I agree with others ... too many eggs and too much bread
I made this per the instructions and they lack flavor. The problem is too much bread. 4 slices is overkill and blunts the taste of the meatballs. Plus too many eggs makes the meatballs like cakes.
I wasn't sure how I would like these Keftedes (Greek Meatballs). But I love these. Will definitely make them again

YUM!!!!! This was a big hit at our house. I halved the eggs in the recipe, and wasn't able to find ground lamb, but it didn't matter, I just used more beef. I am also lazy and baked them in the oven on a rack for about 350F for 30 minutes. (That would vary on the size of your meatballs) I used 90% lean beef, and won't bother with a rack again, since there wasn't any grease. I made them for a Mediterranean potluck. They were devoured! I think adding the lamb would make it better, but not enough to skip making them. I also frozen some raw meatballs to make later. I'll report later on how they turned out. Than you for sharing this delicious recipe, it will be in permanent rotation at my house.
This recipe was delicious! We had it without any sauces. I will definitely be making it again.
